title: cost-optimization: autotune batching/caching defaults + quant profiles + unit-econ tooling
author: Maya Patel
description: Motivation: Reduce per-token unit cost across a broad set of customer workloads by making better defaults and automated tuning available out-of-the-box. This PR implements three coordinated pieces: 1) autotune for batching and KV-prefix caching defaults based on observed latency/cost tradeoffs; 2) first-class quantization profile support in the model registry and runtime selector; 3) a lightweight unit-economics (uecon) CLI and internal API for estimating cost/latency impact of config changes. What changed: - Runtime autopilot: added an autotune module that observes request size distribution and tail latency to compute a recommended default batch_size, window_ms for batching, and cache TTL for prefix/KV caching. - Defaults: shipping tuned defaults.yaml entries for common workload archetypes (chat-short, chat-long, embedding-bulk, rerank) and a bootstrap heuristic for unknown traffic. - Quant profiles: added quant profiles metadata to the model registry and runtime selection logic so we can prefer int8/4-bit profiles where quality/regression budgets allow. - UEcon tooling: new CLI (tools/uecon/cli.py) and internal endpoint (/internal/uecon/v1/estimate) that computes expected token cost, 95th-pct latency, and cost-per-1000-requests for a given config. - Tests & docs: integration tests that validate autotune doesn't regress p99 SLA under synthetic bursts and docs with guidance for ops teams. Checklist: - [x] Design review (ENG-4821) - [x] Perf bench with representative workloads - [x] Integration tests - [x] Docs and quickstart - [x] Rollout plan for existing Dedicated clusters Rollout and safety: Autotune defaults are guarded behind a feature flag (runtime.autotune.enabled) and staged rollout via rollout policies (canary on 5% customer traffic, then 25%, 100%). Quant-profile selection requires an opt-in flag per deployment until model-quality signoff. Impact summary: across our benchmark lab workloads we measured a median unit-cost reduction of 12% and up to 28% for embedding-heavy traffic with negligible median latency change and p95 latency impact <5ms in most cases. Backwards compat: defaults are additive and gated; no breaking changes expected. Related: refactors some config parsing touched in ENG-4970.
